items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: And of course Duke Ellington and Cab Calloway solved that problem.

ctx.x: This is a little off the topic, but so many of the great names have been associated with untimely deaths and jazz seems to have this persona of alcohol and drug abuse. Why did that happen? I mean besides the obvious reasons, you know you’re working in a nightclub, but are there other reasons for it?

Well I mean to me it’s conjecture, I’m not a social historian you know, but as I — I think the musical culture of the 20s, where it started, right, in speakeasies which in turn became nightclubs. Now nightclubs are not, weren’t originally primarily for music, they were places to sell whisky and the music was to lure people in to buy whisky and that’s the atmosphere. So if you were working these incredible hours I don’t think it’s a stretch to get through a night ‘till three or four o’clock in the morning that…
